subject: Discovery recap — CarePoint private hosting & VPC requirements
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Roy <alexandra.roy@carepointhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Apr 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — CarePoint private hosting & VPC requirements

Alexandra, thanks again for the time today — summary and next steps below from our call with your infra and compliance leads. Let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain & goals (what you told us):
- Regulatory scope: handling PHI for telehealth transcripts and embeddings (HIPAA liability).
- Must avoid egress of unencrypted data to public/shared tenants; customer-managed keys (KMS) are required.
- Network constraints: strict inbound/outbound firewall rules, only specific outbound endpoints allowed, and preference for VPC-private deployment (no public internet-facing endpoints).
- Air-gap possibility: for some clinics, an air-gapped on-prem bundle could be required in future procurement phases.

Current stack & constraints:
- Primary cloud: AWS (us-east-1) with centralized transit gateway.
- On-prem clinics run Citrix + local gateways; many sites have limited outbound ports (443 only to approved FQDNs).
- Identity: Okta SSO; current KMS via AWS KMS in customer account.

Success criteria for POC / procurement:
1) Deployment model that supports VPC/private deployment with no plaintext tokenization off-host.
2) Support for customer-managed KMS with key rotation policy agreed.
3) Network allowlist doc + minimal required egress endpoints for a scoped POC.
4) Performance: 95th percentile latency <150ms for inference in the regional VPC.
5) Compliance artifacts: SOC2 Type II report and a runbook for incident response.

Risks / open items we flagged:
- Air-gap requirements may push to a later procurement stage; need to understand which clinics require it.
- Firewall/IP allowlist might be infeasible for clinics with only FQDN-level allowlisting; we'll need to provide FQDN-based options and short-lived certs if required.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
- Monica: send qualification checklist and network inventory template (attached) — today.
- Alexandra / CarePoint infra: send a redacted network diagram + list of sites that will be in scope for the POC — by Wed 4/12.
- Ben: prepare a draft high-level deployment architecture (VPC peering/transit flow + KMS integration options) — EOD Thu 4/13.
- Sean: pull SOC2 docs and our standard KMS/key-handover playbook for review — done by Fri 4/14.

Attachments: redwood-private-qualification-checklist.pdf (checklist), network-inventory-template.xlsx (spreadsheet).

If that matches your understanding, we can lock the POC scope and schedule a technical kickoff the week of 4/17.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
From: Alexandra Roy <alexandra.roy@carepointhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: itsec@carepointhealth.com, procurement@carepointhealth.com
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — CarePoint private hosting & VPC requirements

Monica — thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side:

- KMS: yes, we need AWS KMS in our account. Keys must never be exportable and must be rotated annually. We also need an offline key-escrow process for legal hold scenarios.
- Network: most clinics can only do DNS/FQDN allowlisting (they won't allow static IPs). If you can provide a short list of FQDNs for the POC, that helps.
- Air-gap: currently only 6 rural clinics will be candidates for air-gapped installs; procurement wants a ballpark cost delta versus VPC for budgeting.
- Data residency: all telemetry/usage logs need to be stored in our AWS account in us-east-1; we cannot send logs to Redwood-managed S3.

We will upload a redacted network diagram and an initial list of the 12 sites we want in-scope for the POC by EOD Wed 4/12. Procurement copied here for contracting and budgeting.

Would it be possible to get the minimal egress FQDN list and our SOC2 snapshot this week? That will unblock our infosec review.

--
Alexandra Roy
Director, IT Architecture | CarePoint Health
alexandra.roy@carepointhealth.com | +1 (617) 555-4890
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Roy <alexandra.roy@carepointhealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — CarePoint private hosting & VPC requirements

Thanks Alexandra — noted. Quick replies to your asks:

- FQDN list: we'll provide an FQDN-only allowlist for the POC (certificate pinning + short TTL certs for extra safety). Draft list attached in the checklist PDF; we'll extract a single-page FQDN table as well.
- KMS: we support AWS KMS customer-managed keys in the customer account. We'll include the key-rotation and escrow options in the deployment doc.
- Logs: we can send logs to your S3 bucket in your account and provide role-based access. No telemetry will be stored in Redwood's buckets for the POC unless explicitly agreed.
- Air-gap cost delta: rough estimate: +25-40% single-upfront engineering plus ongoing support premium. We'll formalize once we see the site list.

Next steps I'll own: share the single-page FQDN list and a POC timeline draft by EOD Thu 4/13. Monica will follow with the SOC2 snapshot and qualification checklist this afternoon.

If you want to accelerate, we can schedule a 30-min technical touchpoint with our infra engineer on Thu.

Cheers,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
